judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[F]or amounts and upon terms which Lender considers advisable" is a wholly subjective standard, though the netting mechanic is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.5(f) grants the same settlement power subject to Lender's "Permitted Discretion" — a different and higher standard for the same act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing parenthetical charges amounts as "Lender Group Expenses", a capitalised term that does not exist in this agreement (the defined term is "Lender Expenses").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Lender Expenses are Obligations chargeable to the Loan Account under Sections 2.5(c) and 2.9, an undefined expense category leaves these amounts without a home in the payment waterfall of Section 2.3(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]uch payments and ... such acts as Lender considers necessary or reasonable" is subjective, and the clause refers to "any Guarantor" though there is none.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Lien-compromise power is expressly measured by Lender's Permitted Discretion, matching Section 2.1(b); the Guarantor reference is a loose end shared with the Guarantor definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A set-off right with an express notice waiver and an anti-strict-foreclosure saving; well drafted, though the subclause is mis-lettered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6(d)'s Lien on Cash Management Accounts and Section 9.1(h)'s cash collateral right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cash-collateral right; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps Section 9.1(g)'s set-off right and Section 2.3(b)(F)-(G)'s cash collateral mechanics without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Ship, reclaim, recover, store, finish, maintain, repair, prepare for sale" and the licence over "labels ... and advertising matter" are inventory-finance boilerplate with no application to a portfolio of mortgage notes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrower Collateral definition includes Inventory and IP, so the clause is not inconsistent, but it does not fit a business whose only real collateral is Notes Receivable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sale power measured by what "Lender determines is commercially reasonable"; the Code overlay in the Section 9.1 chapeau limits it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.1's opening Code proviso and Section 9.1(k)'s notice rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 15-day notice rule with the standard perishable/recognised-market exceptions; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notice is to be given "as provided in Section 12", and Section 12 has a special deemed-sent rule for enforcement notices against Borrower Collateral; the two dovetail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subclause is lettered "(h)", duplicating an earlier subclause, and the credit-bid right is limited to public sales although clause (j) contemplates private sales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The public/private asymmetry tracks Code limits, so it is consistent with the Section 9.1 chapeau's Code proviso.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A receiver-appointment right qualified "to the maximum extent permitted by law"; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.2's cumulative-remedies provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A residual remedies catch-all after fourteen specific ones; it is mis-lettered "(m)", duplicating the preceding subclause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.2 says the same thing again, so the catch-all is duplicated rather than in conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It again charges amounts as undefined "Lender Group Expenses", and the appended acceleration paragraph is bolted onto a lettered subclause rather than standing separately.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The acceleration paragraph refers to "Section 8.4 or Section 8.5", which the body of the agreement numbers "3.4" and "3.5", and it largely duplicates Section 9.1(e)'s servicing powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cumulative-remedies and anti-waiver language; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section 15.2 almost exactly, which is redundancy rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lender may act "in its sole discretion and without prior notice", and the closing sentence makes an official notice "conclusive evidence" of validity — strong but clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (b) lets Lender set reserves against the Borrowing Base "as Lender deems necessary", which is inconsistent with Section 2.1(b)'s promise not to establish reserves unless a Triggering Event has occurred and is continuing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional list of waivers; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.13(e)'s broader waivers and Section 9.1's notice waivers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exculpation is expressly conditioned on Lender complying with its Code obligations, which preserves the statutory duty of care; carefully drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2's custodial arrangements and Section 6.8's allocation of insurance risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity expressly covers the Indemnified Person's own negligence in capitals but carves out gross negligence and wilful misconduct — broad, one-sided, but stated with unusual clarity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.11 contains a second, differently worded indemnity (limited to liability "resulting solely from" gross negligence or wilful misconduct), so two indemnities with different carve-outs cover overlapping ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deemed-receipt rule mixes actual receipt with a three-Business-Day mailing presumption and then says facsimile is "as effective" as any other method without stating when it is deemed received.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1(k)(ii) requires 15 days' notice before disposition measured against this Section's rules, and this Section applies a different (deemed-sent) rule to enforcement notices; the interaction requires care but is drafted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear and comprehensive New York choice-of-law clause with an express carve-out for contrary provisions in other Loan Documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.13(g) and (h) waive rights and defences framed entirely by reference to California Code of Civil Procedure sections, and the Code definition selects the New York UCC with a mandatory-law fallback — a live tension over which law supplies the antideficiency rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The venue clause is exclusive against Borrowers but gives Lender an option to sue anywhere collateral is found — a markedly one-sided asymmetry of the kind construed against its drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.3 disclaims construction against either party, which cuts against a contra proferentem reading; the two provisions pull in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mutual jury waiver with representations of knowing consent; standard and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13(b)'s venue provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A $5,000,000 minimum and an Eligible Transferee requirement, both then disapplied for portfolio-level transfers — the carve-out is broad enough to swallow the restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Eligible Transferee definition itself already includes an approval catch-all, so the transfer restrictions are thin; Section 14.2 confirms no Borrower consent is needed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]uch assignment shall effect a novation between Borrowers and the Assignee" is a strong legal characterisation attached to a mechanical transfer; the survival proviso is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the assignor's Section 11.3 and 16.8 obligations, consistent with those sections' own survival language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-executing deemed amendment "to the extent, but only to the extent, necessary"; the limitation is stated but its content is left to inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1 provides that no amendment is effective unless in writing and signed by Lender and Administrative Borrower, which this clause bypasses — a direct clash between two amendment mechanisms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long but tightly enumerated, with five specified matters on which a Participant may be given veto rights and an express denial of direct rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Participants are "Indemnified Persons" under Section 11.3 even though they have no direct rights under this clause — a mild inconsistency in their status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short disclosure permission expressly subject to Section 16.8; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.8(f) contains the matching carve-out requiring recipients to agree to confidentiality; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional Federal Reserve pledge provision with specific regulatory citations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides "[a]ny other provision in this Agreement", which is broader than Section 14.1(a)'s transfer restrictions but expressly so.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A successors clause with an absolute bar on Borrower assignment ("void ab initio"); determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.1's assignment mechanics and Section 7.3's fundamental-changes covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-oral-modification clause carving out Bank Product Agreements; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(c) deems this Agreement amended automatically on an assignment without any signed writing, and several definitions contemplate schedules being "updated from time to time" without amendment formalities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard anti-waiver and cumulative-remedies language; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section 9.2; redundancy without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence tying effectiveness to execution; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1's conditions precedent govern the obligation to lend rather than effectiveness, so the two coexist; the closing conditions are not a condition to the contract's binding force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence — "Unless the contrary is compelled by the context, everything contained in each Section applies equally to this entire Agreement" — is an unusual and potentially far-reaching interpretive instruction whose effect is hard to pin down.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it would carry section-specific limits (for example Section 2.1(b)'s reserve limitation or Section 2.3's priority rule) across the whole instrument, which is in tension with those sections' own scoping language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disclaims any construction against either party and directs construction "according to the ordinary meaning of the words used" — a provision that is itself invoked precisely when there is an ambiguity to resolve.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument is heavily one-sided in Lender's favour (Sections 13(b), 2.1(b), 3.1(u), 9.1), so this anti-contra-proferentem clause does real work against the drafting pattern of the rest of the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says only that provisions are "severable ... for the purpose of determining the legal enforceability of any specific provision" — it never states what happens to the rest of the agreement if one provision fails.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.5(e)'s usury savings clause is the only provision that actually addresses the consequence of unenforceability, and it does so for interest only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines "Taxes" mid-provision with an express net-income exclusion and a gross-up mechanic; long but precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.11 addresses capital-adequacy costs on parallel terms; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Counterparts and electronic execution, with an express saving for failure to deliver originals; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.4's Record provision and Section 16.1's effectiveness rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A revival clause triggered by repayment "or elects to do so upon the reasonable advice of its counsel", which lets Lender revive liability by its own election.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to Guarantors although none exists, and works with Section 2.13(i)'s reinstatement provision; the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Seven enumerated exceptions, most with conditions; the exception in clause (c) for disclosure "as may be required by statute, decision, or judicial or administrative order, rule, or regulation" is broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The two-year survival period sits against Section 14.1(b)'s statement that an assigning Lender remains bound by Section 16.8, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure statutory notice with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No interaction with other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The merger clause bars contradiction only by agreements "before the date hereof", saying nothing about contemporaneous side agreements — a narrower integration clause than it appears.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates "the other Loan Documents", several of which (Servicing Agreement, Validity Agreements, Cash Management Agreements) are not in the record, so the integrated whole extends beyond this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The appointment is "irrevocable" yet the same sentence provides a mechanism for its revocation — an internal tension in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The indemnity here uses "resulted solely from the gross negligence or wilful misconduct", a narrower carve-out than Section 11.3's, and Section 2.8 lets Lender act on instructions from anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person rather than through Administrative Borrower.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The form contains unclosed brackets and blank dates and states a notice period ("not less than 3 Business Days") in bracketed instructional text rather than operative terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address gives zip code 75254 while Section 12's notice provision gives 75244, and Section 2.12(c) makes a Base Rate election the exception rather than the norm this form implies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph 6 refers to "Sections 7.16, and 7.37" — there is no Section 7.37 — and paragraphs 2 and 5 duplicate the same representation bring-down with different carve-outs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is signed by "the undersigned officer of Manager" while the Compliance Certificate definition requires delivery by the chief financial officer of Administrative Borrower, and Schedule 3 tests the 0.9% Senior Leverage Ratio that cannot be met with the facility drawn.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bracketed optional text and blank dates make the form incomplete, and it assumes an affirmative LIBOR election.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(c) makes the LIBOR election automatic absent a contrary notice, so this form's premise conflicts with the deemed-election mechanic; the address zip also differs from Section 12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The account holder is given as "B-4 PARTNER, LLC" rather than B-4 Partners LLC, and the schedule mixes a specific account with an open substitution formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the Designated Account to be subject to a Control Agreement at a bank other than Wells Fargo, while Section 2.6(a) requires all Cash Management Accounts to be at Wells Fargo after 60 days and Section 6.12(d) restricts maintaining other accounts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The account number is illegible/incomplete in the text, but the substitution mechanism is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3(a), 2.6(b)(iii) and 2.7's references to the Lender's Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item 2 permits "the Subordinated Liens securing Approved Debt" without any description of the property, amount or priority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(b)(ii) contemplates Schedule P-1 Liens "specifically identified thereon as entitled to have priority over the Lender's Liens", but the schedule identifies none; and permitting Liens for Approved Debt conflicts with the definition of Subordinated Debt as unsecured Indebtedness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual list of two licences; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 says the schedule lists "all" required licences for both Borrowers, yet only Fund's are listed — a gap between the representation and the schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short entries, one of which is a class description rather than a location.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 represents that Borrower Collateral is not stored with a bailee, yet entry 1 contemplates a custodian holding the notes, and Section 6.9 requires a Collateral Access Agreement for the Lafayette premises which Section 3.1(o) addressed by a landlord waiver.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-line schedule with an added "SUBSIDIARIES - NONE" note; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Subsidiary definition excludes Bar-K, Inc. and New Funds, so "NONE" is consistent, but Schedule 5.8 is separately supposed to list Subsidiaries — a small duplication.
